explanation: Maintain the best nonnegative sum ending at the current entry. A negative suffix is discarded because it cannot improve any future subarray. Starting the answer at zero permits the empty subarray.
timeComplexity: O(n). The scan performs two maximum comparisons per input value and stores no per-index array.
spaceComplexity: O(1). Only the current suffix optimum and global optimum are stored.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: The maintained suffix is the maximum sum among subarrays ending at the current entry, with the empty suffix allowed. A negative suffix cannot help any later extension and is replaced by zero. Every nonempty optimum ends at some entry, so the greatest suffix value, also compared with zero, is the answer.
walkthrough: For [−4,5,−2,3,−7], suffix sums retained by the scan are 0, 5, 3, 6 and 0. The best interval [5,−2,3] has sum 6. The walkthroughCase uses the judge’s JSON input format and expected observation.
edgeCases: All-negative input returns zero because the empty subarray is allowed.
A negative prefix must not burden a later positive run.
